item: Storage guard: "Resume anyway" really overrides the pause (R112), bounded by a floor that protects the drive
key_paths: src/scheduler/storage_guard.py; src/api/scheduler.py; src/static/app-core.js; src/static/taskmanager.js; tests/test_storage_guard.py; tests/storage_guard_node_test.js
summary: The button #1279 shipped only retried. It now resumes collection while a limit is still exceeded (R112, answer 18a) and the override ends by itself when free space falls to max(128 MiB, the log's own size), at once on a write that fails for want of space, and when the cause clears; it is refused with a sentence when free space is at or below that floor, unreadable, or held by a recent write error, lives in memory only, ends too when free space stays unreadable or a second limit it was not granted for trips (the pause then shows with the new numbers), and leaves the drain and the maintenance block running. The notice, the toast and the 'resumed by you' note ship in 12 locales and no stale 'Paused' label sits beside them. Also folds the #1279 check's follow-ups: the disk sentences stop instructing the user, one stated reason for the disk reserve, the supervisor stops at shutdown, a lasting pin is logged once per change, a lapsed write-error hold releases as a retry, wait_if_engaged takes max_wait_s.
